messages.content: Seattle is off my plate. I just got the next rollout: Research Triangle in late March. Can you help me make the first plan before I ask my director for approval? Roughly Monday setup in Cary, Tue/Wed clinic trainings in Durham and Raleigh, and a Thursday skills check near Chapel Hill. I’ll have the rolling demo case this time.

Yes. I’d frame this around protecting the setup day and keeping the driving triangle sane. Before I rank it, do you have firm clinic start times yet, and is the case something you’ll check with the airline or carry/claim at baggage? Also: are you trying to avoid an extra Sunday hotel night, or is reliability the bigger argument?

Times are still squishy. Cary is likely Monday mid to late afternoon, Durham Tuesday morning, Raleigh Wednesday, Chapel Hill Thursday after lunch. I can check the demo case if I have to, but I need to be there when it arrives and I need a car that can actually hold it. The cheaper version is Monday morning travel; the calmer version is Sunday afternoon into RDU. United is fine if it’s the clean itinerary, but I don’t want to force that.

First pass ranking: 1) Sunday afternoon nonstop DEN-RDU, pick up the car at RDU, sleep in Cary. It adds one hotel night, but it gives you Monday morning to handle baggage, car fit, demo inventory, and a buffer before setup. 2) Monday very-early nonstop only if the Cary setup is after 3:00 and the fare gap is meaningful. A delay or baggage issue would hit the client day. 3) Sunday one-stop if savings are large and the layover is simple. With the demo case, I’d avoid two stops or anything with a tight connection.
That makes sense. For the director, assume I need to justify Sunday. Where should I sleep? I don’t know if Cary, Durham, or airport is smartest.

Rank the zones this way until the clinic map is final: 1) Central Cary or west Raleigh is the best balance for Monday setup and not awful for Durham, Raleigh, or Chapel Hill. It also helps if you need to run back to the hotel between sites. 2) Durham or RTP is attractive if Tuesday is the earliest start or the hotel is much better, but it adds Monday cross-town driving with the case. 3) RDU airport is useful only for a late arrival or early departure; otherwise it makes the week feel like a commute from the wrong base.
I’d like a well-reviewed place, at least around 4.0 if we can tell, and I’d use a pool and gym. Hot tub would be nice after standing all day, but don’t send me way off route just for that.

Then I’d shortlist a Cary suite property first if it has strong guest scores, parking, a pool, and fitness access; a Durham extended-stay second if it has the full pool, hot tub, and gym set plus clearly better reviews; and an airport hotel only as the budget fallback. For this trip, location probably beats the hot tub because you’re moving the demo case daily.
Rental car: what category would you put in the plan? I don’t want to discover at baggage claim that the case won’t fit.

Book at least an intermediate SUV or midsize SUV, not a compact. Pickup Sunday evening at RDU; return after the final airport drop. Add a note for fold-flat rear seats, and keep a photo of the case dimensions in the reservation notes. If the case is checked, build in 45 minutes after landing before any real commitment.
Good. Give me the confirmation list I need from the clients before I let you book anything.

Ask for exact addresses and room locations for all four sites; Monday setup start and end window; Tuesday first-session start in Durham; whether the demo case can be left securely overnight at any site; parking or loading instructions; badge and after-hours access rules; who signs for the skills-check materials near Chapel Hill; and whether any site requires proof of equipment cleaning. Director rationale: Sunday nonstop into RDU plus a Cary base reduces delay risk, protects the demo case handoff, and keeps the first client day from depending on a same-day flight.

messages.content: I have firm times for the Triangle week now: Cary setup Monday at 3:30, Durham Tuesday 8:30, Raleigh Wednesday, and Chapel Hill wraps Thursday around 2:45, maybe 3:15. Can we make the booking choices instead of keeping three versions alive?

Yes. That timing points to the Sunday afternoon nonstop into RDU and a Cary hotel. Monday travel is still technically possible, but it gives you almost no cushion for baggage, rental-car fit, or setup. For the return, the open question is whether you want to push for Thursday night or make Friday the low-stress exit.
I don’t love staying Thursday night, but I also don’t want a rental-car sprint from Chapel Hill with the demo case. What does Thursday look like?

If the wrap is 2:45, a 6:30-ish nonstop could work on paper: 35 to 45 minutes to RDU, fuel, rental return, bag drop, and security. If it slips to 3:15, it becomes fragile. I’d only use Thursday if the client agrees to a hard stop and the fare is much better.
Let’s do the calmer version: Sunday in, Friday home. Pick the Cary suite hotel even though it lacks the hot tub, as long as parking is easy and the rating is solid.

Book it as: DEN-RDU Sunday afternoon nonstop; RDU-DEN Friday late morning or midday nonstop if available; Cary suite hotel Sunday through Thursday nights; midsize SUV pickup at RDU Sunday evening and return Friday before the flight. Confirm hotel parking is included or reimbursable, and request a room away from the elevator with enough floor space for the case.
For seats, take a window if there’s one free, but don’t spend extra unless it’s minor. Also remind me what to do with the demo case.

Booking order: 1) hold the flights, then select free or low-cost window seats if available; 2) reserve the Cary hotel with flexible cancellation and parking noted; 3) book the midsize SUV with Sunday evening pickup and Friday drop-off; 4) add one checked demo case to the outbound and return, photograph the packed case, label it inside and outside, and carry the irreplaceable small instruments with you; 5) send the director the Sunday-buffer rationale and the no-hot-tub tradeoff.

messages.content: Problem: Chapel Hill added a Friday debrief that could run to 11:30. My booked Friday midday RDU-DEN return now looks tight. Move it or add Saturday?

Move it. Midday leaves too little time for the drive, fuel, rental return, bag drop, and security. Choices: later Friday one-stop gets you home late; Saturday morning nonstop is easier but adds hotel and car nights.
The later Friday option is 4:55 RDU-IAH-DEN, 68-minute layover, lands 9:40. Saturday nonstop is 9:30 a.m. I’d rather be home Friday if that connection isn’t dumb.
With a 68-minute same-carrier layover, it’s workable, not luxurious. It becomes much better if the demo case ships back from Chapel Hill instead of connecting with you.
They can ship the case Friday afternoon. Let’s take the later Friday connection and keep checkout Friday.

Do that. Steps: change to the 4:55 Friday one-stop, keep the Cary hotel through Friday checkout only, move SUV return to about 2:30-3:00, get the case shipping label and pickup contact in writing, and tell Chapel Hill you can stay until 11:30 but need to leave by noon.
